searches.note: Twenty searches of twenty eight, eight unspent. Most searches blocked the author's domains so the second source would be independent; four were held to a house's own domain to read its sheets. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source or none it was cut or hedged.

tested: 1940 and the start as a branch of La Caroyense of Colonia Caroya (Economía Solidaria, Rutacoop, the co-operative's own account on X, searched without the author's domains): sound; the separation of 30 June 1989 found and added.
Fairtrade 2006 and the Tilimuqui school (the house's Fairtrade pages, Wines of Argentina news of 28 May 2010, Fairtrade International): sound; first pupils March 2010, inaugurated 12 May 2010.

Santa Florentina smelter and the cable way from La Mejicana (the national heritage page, Alpinismonline, Ruta del Mate): sound; the cable way ran from late 1905 to 1927, and the ore went on to the Santa Florentina smelter.

The making: cold settling 24 to 36 hours at 8 to 10 degrees, ferment at 16 to 18 with the house's selected yeast LRV 945 (the house's Santa Florentina sheet, read through search on lariojana.com.ar): sound.
Tilimuqui as the organic Fairtrade range named for the village seven kilometres from the winery (la-riojana.squarespace.com; a critic's listing under Famatina): sound.

The Malbec (the house's product page): plum and black pepper, full bodied and velvety, 14 to 16 degrees; the Malbec Reserva in French oak.

swapRulings: San Huberto: the author's proposed rename to Nina Torrontés, Valle de Aminga, is refused. No house sheet exists for either wine; Nina is sold in tiers (Nina, Nina Gold) whose notes come from critics and a competition, so a rename would rest no better and would pick one tier on no ground. The record now teaches Valle de Aminga in its label question and its story, which serves the guest the same. Vista Larga: the author proposed no swap and kept the pick; ruled kept: the house's own site, which the author did not find, now sources its place, its note and its service, and its valley's indication of 2026 makes it worth teaching. No change to plan.json.
planNotes: chanarmuyo why: 'planted from 2001' should read begun in 2001 (land bought at the end of 2001, planting later).
vista-larga why: 'the one planting of its valley by press account' should read the first extensive planting by its own account, at about 1,250 metres.
valle-de-la-puerta why: 'Torrontés was the first grape it planted' stays unsourced, as the author found.
codexTension: The region summary calls Torrontés Riojano 'the finest of the three Torrontés', a ranking; reported, not edited.

The region's producers line calls La Riojana the province's biggest producer and one of the world's leading Fairtrade sources, and Chañarmuyo's line speaks of its Torrontés, which no source confirmed; reported, not edited.
questionsChecked: Ten questions read: each has one right answer and four options of one kind. San Huberto's wine question replaced (its key leaned on an Aminga range that is one red); Chañarmuyo's story stem reworded to the purchase of 2001; explanations of La Riojana, Valle de la Puerta and Vista Larga set right to their sources.
